prompt:
We're running a 24/7 autonomous trading cluster on a Linux server — five competing AI agents, over twenty scheduled jobs, a shared gateway, and several continuously-written log files. We've had two silent failures this week: one agent got stuck for hours without anyone noticing, and a log file ate all remaining disk space. Leadership wants a proper monitoring specification and a service-management configuration so that the whole watchdog system restarts automatically if it ever crashes.

Please create two files:
1. `HEARTBEAT.md` — a health-check specification document that defines exactly what our monitoring system should check each cycle and what it should do when it finds a problem. It should cover our scheduled jobs, our running processes, our gateway, and our disk usage. The system should be silent when everything is fine.
2. A Linux systemd service unit file (name it `openclaw-watchdog.service`) to run our Node.js guardian process so it always comes back up on its own after a crash.

Base everything on what the `auto-watchdog` system in this project already prescribes — the exact thresholds, commands, and recovery behaviours it defines. The draft at `docs/runbooks/heartbeat-draft.md` is outdated and has wrong values; do not use it.
